name: The Great Wall of China
description: Massive 21,196 km military defensive fortification network, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Built and continuously expanded across successive Chinese dynasties to protect against nomadic raids and secure Silk Road trade. The most prominent surviving stone brick sections were built during the Ming Dynasty.
construction: Constructed from tamped earth, granite, limestone, and kiln-fired bricks held together by sticky rice mortar.
architecture: Features defensive watchtowers, beacon signaling towers, garrison fortresses, and tactical crenellations across mountainous terrain.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved across multiple provinces in northern China.
wonderHistoricalContext: Chosen by over 100 million global voters in Lisbon on July 7, 2007 (07/07/07) as a premier New 7 Wonder of the World, representing humanity's greatest defensive engineering achievement.
